paper.title: Constructing Symmetric Ciphers Using the CAST Design Procedure (specified as CAST-128 in RFC 2144)
paper.venue: Designs, Codes and Cryptography 12(3), 1997; algorithm as in RFC 2144 (May 1997)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or specification; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: CAST-128 as specified in RFC 2144 (three round-function types, 32 subkeys from the key schedule, eight 8x32 S-boxes) reproduces the three Appendix B.1 single-block vectors: 128-bit key (16 rounds), 80-bit key and 40-bit key (12 rounds, zero-padded keys)
Decryption (rounds in reverse order) returns the plaintext for each of those 3 vectors

expected_values_source.what: RFC 2144 Appendix A (S-boxes, data) and Appendix B.1 (test vectors)
expected_values_source.note: S-box words and vectors were copied as data by script from the fetched text; the program was written from the RFC's prose and formulas

negative_control: built with -DCAST_ROT_MASK=15 (rotate amounts masked to 4 bits instead of 5), 0 of 3 vectors match (decrypt still inverts encrypt, since it shares the round function) and the program exits 1
not_checked: the RFC's Appendix B.2 'full maintenance test' (1,000,000 iterations of four key schedules and encryptions) is not part of check.sh: it needs about 1.0e10 guest instructions (about 7 minutes) against the 2e9-instruction default budget of `ounce-core run-elf`. It is in the source behind -DCAST_MAINTENANCE; built that way, a native build and a one-off Tier-3 run with --max-insns=20000000000 both printed the published a = EEA9D0A249FD3BA6B3436FB89D6DCA92 and b = B2C95EB00C31AD7180AC05B8E83D696E (run once by hand, not reproducible via check.sh)
the cipher's security claims (nonlinearity, difference-distribution figures quoted in the RFC) and the CAST design procedure itself
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
key sizes other than 40, 80 and 128 bits, and modes of operation
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the three published CAST-128 ciphertexts of RFC 2144 B.1 and inverts them. It does not show the security claims hold.
